questions.question: You need to determine the immediate medical response for a worker exposed to a chemical. In which section of the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) should you look?

Given that Methane has a Lower Flammable Limit (LFL) of 5.0% and an Upper Flammable Limit (UFL) of 15.0%. An air sample taken from a confined space measures a Methane concentration of \( 30,000\ \mathrm{ppm} \). Which statement accurately describes the condition of this atmosphere?

choices.D: Immediately Dangerous to Life and Health (IDLH)

questions.question: A gas mixture consists of 50% Methane (LFL = 5.0) and 50% Propane (LFL = 2.1) by volume. Most nearly, what is the Lower Flammable Limit (LFL) of this mixture?
A worker is entering a grain bin for maintenance. Which of the following is a primary physical hazard specifically highlighted for this environment?

choices.B: Engulfment or entrapment in flowing grain

references: Refer to FE Reference Handbook 10.5 – Page 21

questions.question: A worker comes into contact with a 60-Hz AC electrical circuit. According to the “Effects of Electrical Current on the Human Body” table, which current range corresponds to the “Let-go” threshold where a person can still voluntarily release the energized conductor?
Which of the following substances represents the highest toxicity (lowest lethal dose)?

A worker’s forearms (Surface Area \( SA = 2,000\ \mathrm{cm^2} \)) are in contact with wastewater containing a chemical at a concentration of \( 5.0\ \mathrm{mg/L} \). The chemical-specific permeability constant (\( PC \)) is \( 0.001\ \mathrm{cm/hr} \). The exposure occurs for 1 hour/day (\( ET \)), 250 days/year (\( EF \)) over 10 years (\( ED \)). The worker’s body weight (\( BW \)) is 70 kg, and the averaging time (\( AT \)) is 3,650 days (10 years). Using the handbook formula for Dermal contact with water, most nearly, what is the Absorbed Dose (AD)?

A chemical has a Cancer Slope Factor of \( 0.055\ (\mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day})^{-1} \). If a resident’s calculated Chronic Daily Intake (CDI) is \( 0.004\ \mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day} \), most nearly, what is the estimated incremental lifetime cancer risk?

A chronic toxicity study establishes a No-Observed-Adverse-Effect Level (NOAEL) of \( 50\ \mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day} \) for a substance. To derive a human Reference Dose (RfD), uncertainty factors for interspecies variation (\( 10 \)) and intraspecies variation (\( 10 \)) are applied. Most nearly, what is the resulting RfD?

A child (15 kg) plays in soil contaminated with lead at a concentration of \( 400\ \mathrm{mg/kg} \). The child ingests \( 200\ \mathrm{mg} \) of soil per day for 350 days per year over a 6-year period. Assume the fraction ingested from the contaminated source (FI) is 1.0. Most nearly, what is the Chronic Daily Intake (CDI) for this child over the exposure duration?

Workers in a facility are exposed to toluene vapors. The average daily intake concentration is calculated to be \( 0.03\ \mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day} \). The Reference Dose (RfD) for toluene is \( 0.08\ \mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day} \). Most nearly, what is the Hazard Index (HI) for this exposure?

A groundwater supply is contaminated with arsenic at a concentration of \( 0.05\ \mathrm{mg/L} \). An adult resident (70 kg) consumes 2.0 L of this water daily for 20 years. The Cancer Slope Factor (CSF) for arsenic is \( 1.5\ (\mathrm{mg/kg\text{-}day})^{-1} \). Assume the averaging time for carcinogens is 70 years (25,550 days). Most nearly, what is the excess lifetime cancer risk for this resident?
\( 1.5 \times 10^{-5} \)

\( 6.1 \times 10^{-4} \)

\( 4.3 \times 10^{-4} \)

\( 2.1 \times 10^{-3} \)
A waste stream containing Cyanides (Group 11) is accidentally mixed with a waste stream containing Mineral Acids (Group 1). What are the potential consequences of this mixture?

choices.C: Generation of Toxic and Flammable Gas (GT, GF)

questions.question: An engineer is evaluating metal materials for a tank containing Hydrochloric Acid. Which of the following metals exhibits the lowest corrosion rate?

questions.question: A process generates solvent vapor at a mass rate of \( Q_m = 20\ \mathrm{g/min} \). The solvent has a molecular weight (\( M \)) of \( 100\ \mathrm{g/mol} \). The operation takes place at \( T = 298\ \mathrm{K} \) (\( 25^\circ\mathrm{C} \)) and \( P = 1\ \mathrm{atm} \). The mixing factor (\( k \)) is 1.0. Given the Ideal Gas Constant \( R = 0.08206\ \mathrm{L \cdot atm / (mol \cdot K)} \), to maintain the concentration below the PEL of \( 500\ \mathrm{ppm} \), the required ventilation rate \( Q_v \) is most nearly:

A worker performs a lifting task with the following measurements:
Horizontal distance (\( H \)) = 20 inches

Vertical location (\( V \)) = 30 inches

Vertical travel distance (\( D \)) = 10 inches

Asymmetry angle (\( A \)) = 0 degrees

Frequency Multiplier (\( FM \)) = 0.90

Coupling Multiplier (\( CM \)) = 1.00
What is the Recommended Weight Limit (RWL)?

A worker performs a lifting task with a frequency of 1 lift per minute (\( F = 1 \)). The duration of the task is 45 minutes. The vertical location of the hands is 20 inches. What is the Frequency Multiplier (FM)?

A plant records 3 lost-time cases and 2 restricted duty cases over a period where the total hours worked (\( T \)) is 200,000. Most nearly, what is the rate for these cases (commonly known as the DART rate)?
A plant with 100 employees (Total hours worked \( T = 200,000 \)) has 8 recordable incidents. Most nearly, what is the Total injury/illness incidence rate (IR)?
Two identical noise sources each produce a sound pressure level of \( 85\ \mathrm{dBA} \). Most nearly, what is the total sound pressure level when both operate together?
A worker is exposed to \( 90\ \mathrm{dBA} \) for 4 hours and \( 95\ \mathrm{dBA} \) for 3 hours. Mst nearly, what is the total noise dose \( D \)?

A pump operating as a point source generates a sound pressure level (SPL) of \( 92\ \mathrm{dBA} \) at a distance of \( 10\ \mathrm{ft} \). Most nearly, what is the sound pressure level at a distance of \( 40\ \mathrm{ft} \)?
